key_terms.gloss: being bored WITH something — the second, surface-occupied / depth-hollow form of boredom; the boring arises from Dasein itself, not from a determinate thing
casualness — abandoning oneself (sich überlassen) to being-there-alongside things; an obstructive casualness that is a more profound being-left-empty
being-left-empty transformed: here an emptiness first FORMS itself (the leaving-behind of our proper self), rather than merely remaining unfilled

key_terms.term: Hingehaltenheit (held in limbo to standing time)
key_terms.gloss: being-held-in-limbo transformed: not detained by time-as-dragging but held by time in its STANDING, the stretched standing 'now' that does not release us
leaving ourselves behind — the twofold casualness leaves our proper self standing while we slip away toward what is happening
the indeterminate, unfamiliar thing that bores us; identical with the stretched standing 'now' that sets us in place even as we slip away
being entirely present (ganz Gegenwart) to what is happening; the making-present that brings the time taken to a stand and grounds the unity of the two moments
time brought to a stand: sealing-off of having-been and unbinding of future dissolve the flowing sequence of nows into a single stretched 'now' that stands into Dasein

the ambiguous 'having time' may harbor a greater balance/security of Dasein; 'having no time' may be the deepest lostness in banality

claims.claim: Grasping the intrinsic unity (the structural link / Fuge) of being-held-in-limbo and being-left-empty requires grasping boredom MORE ORIGINALLY, which means moving to a more profound second form.
Depth, not objective span of time, decides the extent of boredom; one can be more bored in five minutes of company than in four hours at the station.

In the second form passing-the-time is not absent, hidden, or repressed but transformed: it is no longer an isolated occupation but the entire comportment — the whole evening of the invitation itself.
In the second form there is no determinate boring thing; what bores us has the character of an 'I know not what', and we ourselves slip into a strange casualness regarding it.

Casualness (Lässigkeit) is a being-left-empty that becomes more profound: it obstructs in advance the very seeking-to-be-satisfied-by-beings, so emptiness grows from the depths rather than from absent fullness.
The being-left-empty here is a self-forming emptiness — an emptiness that first forms itself as the leaving-behind of our proper self; this self-forming emptiness IS the 'I know not what'.

Because we leave ourselves time for the evening, time does not drag and cannot bind us as dragging; instead, by making-present we bring time to a stand — the now is stretched into a single standing 'now'.

Being entirely present (ganz Gegenwart) seals off having-been and unbinds the future, dissolving them into the mere present; the now, cut off on both sides, becomes stuck and stretches itself, standing into Dasein.
Standing time does not release us but summons us and sets us in place — this not-being-released is the sought-after being-held-in-limbo, a MORE ORIGINARY holding-in-limbo than mere dragging.

The structural unity of the two moments is grounded in a making-present that brings the time taken to a stand; the self-forming emptiness both leaves us empty AND holds us in limbo, so the two are one.

Boredom springs from the temporality of Dasein — from a determinate way our own temporality temporalizes itself; this confirms the thesis that boredom is possible only because every Dasein has its time.
In the second form what is boring does NOT come from outside: it arises out of Dasein itself; it is therefore less situation-bound, the surrounding beings being only the occasion on which it arises.

Having-time vs having-no-time is essentially ambiguous: the 'having no time' that looks like rigorous seriousness may be the deepest lostness in the banalities of Dasein, so depth cannot be read off the time-relation alone but only off boredom's own constitution.

Seven points summarize the distinctions in depth between form I (becoming bored by) and form II (being bored with); the seventh: in I boredom arrives extrinsically from an environment, in II it arises within and from out of Dasein on the occasion of a situation.
